### J-6 A drill-down the model drops on a re-run is lost, and then its SVG is deleted
- quote: "On a re-run keep the old source and images lines and every `## Drill-down: ` section below the diagrams, unchanged (FR-25)."
- quote: "and that this run will not draw: no current diagram section's name (step 4) and no image a `## Drill-down: ` section links"
- quote: "it SHALL never delete a drill-down section's SVG"
- situation (risk-rollback): on a re-run, the model rewrites explainer.md and leaves out a `## Drill-down:` section. The human drove that drill-down interactively, and the text is now gone with no copy. Then `nio explain finish` runs step 3. No section links the drill-down's image any more and no current section has its name, but the old images line still lists it, so the SVG is deleted. If it was never committed, it cannot be recovered. TC-9 is e2e and only proves the case where the model keeps the section.
- fix: before the skill rewrites explainer.md, have `finish` (or a new step) record the drill-down headings. Have `finish` refuse, writing nothing and deleting nothing, when a previously recorded drill-down heading is missing. Add an integration test: an explainer whose drill-down was removed after a first `finish`; a second `finish` exits 1 and the drill-down's SVG is byte-unchanged.
- validation: confirmed: CT-5 step 3 deletes a listed SVG when no current section or drill-down link names it, and step 4/5 list drill-down images; a drill-down section the model drops leaves its SVG deletable, and only the skill text (not finish) guards the section; TC-9 covers only the kept case.
- disposition: plan-fix by grill: Human Q15: finish records drill-down headings and refuses before writing or deleting if one is missing (CT-5, TC-43)

### J-7 `finish` alone clears the stale record without redrawing anything
- quote: "then replaces the source lines with one per spec.md, plan.md and contracts.md"
- quote: "`nio explain finish .nio/specs/checkout-refunds/explainer.md`, then `nio status`"
- quote: "Regenerating the explainer on its own when the plan changes; it is only flagged stale."
- situation (risk-rollback): the plan changes and `nio status` flags the explainer as stale. Someone runs `nio explain finish`, as TC-29 and QS-4 step 2 do. The source hashes are overwritten with today's, so the stale line disappears, but the diagrams still show the old plan. Nothing records the drift any more (only the drill-down marker hints at it), and a developer now trusts an explainer the plan has outgrown. This is the misuse UJ-1 names.
- fix: have `finish` refresh the hashes only when the diagram sections' text changed since the last finish (store a hash of that text alongside the source lines), or behind an explicit flag the skill passes. Change TC-29 and QS-4 to show that `finish` alone keeps the stale line, and that only a redraw clears it.
- validation: confirmed: CT-5 step 2 overwrites the source hashes unconditionally and TC-29 and QS-4 assert that finish alone clears the stale line, though nothing checks the diagrams were redrawn.
- disposition: plan-fix by grill: Human Q16: finish refreshes source hashes only after a diagram changed, else prints still stale (CT-5, TC-29, TC-44, QS-4)

### J-8 An older nio reads the "Read first" line as an edit to the approved plan
- quote: "makes `Read first: [explainer.md](explainer.md)` the first line of quickstart.md's body, once"
- quote: "`flow.judged_blob` and `flow.scan` compare quickstart.md through `planned` as they do tasks.md."
- situation (risk-rollback): one clone, with the new nio, runs `@nio:explain` and commits quickstart.md with the line. Another clone still has the old nio. Its `flow.scan` compares quickstart.md by its raw `hash-object`, sees a plan-gate file edited after approval, and sends the effort back to `plan_jury` with a `back` line. That line goes into the append-only history, which only `nio flow` writes and no one can retract by hand. FR-17 says the explainer must never do this. No test covers mixed versions, and the plan says nothing about it.
- fix: state the minimum nio version for an effort whose quickstart carries the line, for example by having `finish` refuse unless the flow state was written by a nio that knows CT-9. Or say plainly in the plan that a mixed-version team must upgrade first, and add a test showing that removing the line by hand restores a byte-identical quickstart (the way back).
- validation: confirmed: quickstart.md is a plan-gate file, and flow.judged_blob compares non-tasks files by raw hash-object, so an older nio sees the Read first line as an edit; CT-9 and the plan say nothing on mixed versions and no test covers it.
- disposition: accepted-risk by human: Accept as risk: single user, nio ships with the repo, so mixed versions are unlikely; if it happens the effort goes back to the plan jury once.

### J-9 It is not stated whether `finish` can be re-run after stopping halfway
- quote: "deletes each SVG the old images line lists that sits in the explainer's own folder"
- quote: "running `npx -y MERMAID -i <temp .mmd> -o <out>` with `subprocess.run`"
- situation (risk-rollback): step 3 deletes orphan SVGs, then step 4 renders. Each render spawns `npx`, which can hang while fetching 382 MB and has no timeout. If `finish` is interrupted or killed during step 4, the explainer on disk still has its old images line and links, which point at files already deleted. The contract does not say whether the file is written once at the end or step by step. It also does not say whether step 3 treats an already-missing listed file as done or fails with `FileNotFoundError`. If it fails, every later `finish` fails. No test re-runs `finish` after a partial one.
- fix: in CT-5, say that the explainer is written once, atomically (temp file plus `os.replace`), and that a listed file already gone is skipped silently. Give CT-3's `subprocess.run` a timeout that maps to `unreachable`. Add a test: an images line listing a missing `explainer-x.svg`; `finish` exits 0 and prints no `deleted:` line for it.
- validation: confirmed: CT-5 does not say whether the explainer is written once or stepwise, nor how step 3 treats an already-missing listed file, and CT-3 gives subprocess.run no timeout; no test re-runs finish after a partial one.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: finish writes once at the end, skips already-gone images, npx has a 120 s timeout; TC-45

### J-10 Image names can collide and overwrite another section's or another topic's SVG
- quote: "renders each Mermaid section's block (CT-3) to `<stem>-<title slug>.svg` beside the explainer"
- quote: "whose name starts `<stem>-` (`explainer-` in plan mode)"
- quote: "then `-explainer-2.md`, `-3` and on"
- situation (risk-rollback): in `.nio/research/`, the stem `<date>-x-explainer` is a prefix of `<date>-x-explainer-2`. If the first file has a section titled `2 Overview`, its image is `<date>-x-explainer-2-overview.svg`, which is exactly the second file's `Overview` image. Rendering silently overwrites the other explainer's image, and a later orphan delete removes it. In the same way, two sections whose titles slug the same overwrite each other in one run.
- fix: have step 4 refuse, or add a numeric suffix to, a target name that another section in this run already uses, or that exists on disk without being listed in this explainer's images line. Use a separator that a slug cannot start with (for example `<stem>--<title slug>.svg`).
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: Images named <stem>--<title slug>.svg with -2, -3 on clash; TC-46

### J-11 The orphan-delete test never checks that the drill-down's image survives
- quote: "an SVG for the drill-down section exists"
- quote: "the drill-down SVG, README.md and notes.svg unchanged"
- quote: "whose name starts `<stem>-` (`explainer-` in plan mode)"
- situation (test-proof): Finish deletes `explainer-drill-1.svg` because it ignores the "no image a `## Drill-down: ` section links" rule. Step 4 then renders the drill-down block to `explainer-drill-down-one.svg`, so "an SVG for the drill-down section exists" still holds and TC-10 passes. That is exactly the deletion FR-26 forbids. The test also lists no in-folder SVG without the `explainer-` prefix, so a dropped prefix check is not caught either: `../../README.md` fails the folder check anyway.
- fix: assert that `explainer-drill-1.svg` is byte-unchanged and still named in the images line. Add a listed in-folder `other.svg` and assert that it survives with its warning.
- validation: confirmed: TC-10 asserts only "an SVG for the drill-down section exists", which a re-render under another name satisfies even if explainer-drill-1.svg was deleted; it also has no listed in-folder SVG lacking the prefix.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: TC-10 asserts drill-down SVG bytes unchanged and a listed other.svg survives with a warning
